title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): A is an ordinary abelian variety of dimension g over a perfect field k of characteristic p, probably finite. A* is the dual abelian variety. T_p(A) is the Tate module of the p-divisible group, an extension 0 -> T_p(A)_rad -> T_p(A) -> T_p(A)_et -> 0. Cartier duality gives T_p(A)_rad ≅ D(T_p(A*)_et). Over a perfect base, T_p(A)_et and T_p(A*)_et therefore determine T_p(A). The page looks for a p-adic analogue of a classical ℓ-adic fact.

(1) Target statement (top line): a canonical isomorphism det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A*)_et. Both are free Z_p-modules of rank g, with Galois or Frobenius action.

(2) The ℓ-adic model (ℓ ≠ p). There is a canonical isomorphism α_ℓ: det T_ℓ(A) ≅ det T_ℓ(A*) ≅ Z_ℓ(g), coming from the Weil pairing T_ℓ(A*) ≅ T_ℓ(A)^∨(1); a crossed-out line records this duality. Choose a polarization φ with associated isogeny φ̃: A -> A*. Then β_ℓ(φ) := det T_ℓ(φ̃): det T_ℓ(A) -> det T_ℓ(A*) has ℓ-adic valuation v_ℓ(deg φ̃), because coker T_ℓ(φ̃) = ker(φ̃)[ℓ^∞]. Grothendieck asserts α_ℓ = β_ℓ(φ)/deg φ.

(3) The p-adic definition 'inspired by this formula'. Set β_p(φ) := det(T_p(φ̃)_et): det T_p(A)_et -> det T_p(A*)_et. Then set α_p(φ) := β_p(φ)/√(deg φ̃), as a map after tensoring with Q_p.
- The square root is forced. ker φ̃ is self-dual under the Weil pairing, and A is ordinary, so ker φ̃[p^∞] = (étale part) × (multiplicative part) with the two parts Cartier dual to each other.
- Hence the étale part has order √(p-part of deg φ̃), and β_p/√deg is a p-adic unit up to sign.
- deg φ̃ is a perfect square for a polarization (deg = χ(L)^2), so √deg is an integer.

(4) Claim to prove: (a) α_p(φ) does not depend on φ. If so, it would give a canonical, Galois-equivariant (since φ is defined over k) identification det T_p(A)_et ⊗ Q_p ≅ det T_p(A*)_et ⊗ Q_p.

(5) A crossed-out attempted lemma. For any endomorphism u, it claimed deg u is a perfect square and det T_p(u)_et = √(deg u), a positive integer. Grothendieck marks it 'faux'. It is indeed false: Frobenius on an ordinary elliptic curve has degree p (not a square) and acts by a unit on the étale part.

(6) The next page repairs this. Any other (anti-)polarization is ψ̃ = φ̃∘u with u in End⁰(A) symmetric for the Rosati involution. Write Δ = det on the étale Tate module and δ = √deg.
- Independence of the polarization reduces to Δ(u) = δ(u) for Rosati-symmetric u.
- The argument gives Δ(u)^2 = deg u, hence Δ(u) = ±δ(u).
- The sign is to be settled by positivity (u = Σ u_i u_i').
- He notes that deg u is a square when u = u'. This is the classical fact that the characteristic polynomial of a symmetric element is a square.

The problem served: describing ordinary abelian varieties (over finite fields) by p-adic linear algebra on T_p(A)_et and T_p(A*)_et. This is close in time and spirit to Serre–Tate and to Deligne's 1969 description of ordinary abelian varieties over finite fields. Here the step is a p-adic substitute for the determinant of the Weil pairing.
errors: The target of α_p is written '⊗ Q_ℓ'. It should be ⊗ Q_p, since the modules are Z_p-modules (a slip, or a misreading of the subscript).

The crossed-out lemma (det T_p(u)_et = √deg u for every endomorphism u) is false, as Grothendieck himself notes ('faux'). It holds at best up to sign for Rosati-symmetric u, which is the route taken on the next page.
The top line omits the subscript 'ét' on T_p(A*). Only the étale parts have rank g, so the intended statement is det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A*)_et.
Independence of φ and the sign are left unproved on this page. Even over Q_p, the result is canonical only once the sign ± is fixed by a positivity argument, which is only sketched on the next page.

The formula α_ℓ = β_ℓ(φ)/deg φ is asserted without justification. The normalization by deg (valuation v_ℓ(deg)) is consistent; the sign and canonicity rest on the Weil-pairing/Pfaffian comparison, which is not written out.

ideas.what: Canonical identification of det T_ℓ(A) with det T_ℓ(A*) (≅ Z_ℓ(g)) via the Weil pairing, expressed through any polarization as det T_ℓ(φ̃)/deg φ̃
ideas.modern_name: Weil pairing / Pfaffian determinant of the Tate module
ideas.where_published: Related material on the Weil pairing appears in SGA 7 (exposé on biextensions); this exact formula is unsure

ideas.what: For ordinary A, the étale p-adic Tate module of the kernel of a polarization has order √(deg) by self-duality, and one normalizes det T_p(φ̃)_et by √deg φ̃
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the p-divisible group of an ordinary abelian variety; Cartier self-duality of the kernel of a polarization

ideas.what: Proposed canonical, Galois-equivariant isomorphism det T_p(A)_et ⊗Q_p ≅ det T_p(A*)_et ⊗Q_p, independent of the polarization: a p-adic analogue of the determinant of the Weil pairing
ideas.modern_name: Determinant of unit-root (étale) Tate modules of ordinary abelian varieties

ideas.what: For Rosati-symmetric u, deg u is a square and det of u on T_p(A)_et equals ±√deg u, with the sign fixed by positivity
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic polynomial of symmetric endomorphisms is a square (a reduced-norm / Pfaffian phenomenon)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Mumford, Abelian Varieties §21 for the square property)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a canonical p-adic determinant isomorphism det T_p(A)_et ≅ det T_p(A*)_et for ordinary abelian varieties, normalized by √deg of a polarization. He reduces independence of the polarization to a sign question (Δ(u) = +√deg u for positive symmetric u), which he does not settle.
missed.quote: α_p(φ) = β_p(φ)/√deg φ̃ ... À prouver : a) α_p(φ) ne dépend pas de φ.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small, concrete question about integral or rational canonical structures on unit-root Tate modules of ordinary abelian varieties, related to Deligne's linear-algebra description of ordinary abelian varieties. Of minor interest: the statement is elementary once the square-root/positivity argument is completed, and it is likely implicit in later work.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but fairly elementary working notes: a p-adic analogue of the Weil-pairing determinant for ordinary abelian varieties, with a false lemma crossed out and a sign issue left open. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's thinking about ordinary abelian varieties around 1969, but does not contain a result a specialist would find surprising.
transcription_corrections: Top line: the right-hand side is 'dét T_p(A*)'. In context it should carry the subscript 'ét'.
'Si on a ℓ ≠ p — bien ou [?] p' is better read as something like 'Si on a ℓ ≠ p — bien connu —, on a bien ...'. It is a remark that the ℓ-adic case is well known.
Crossed-out line: 'car T_ℓ(A*) ≃ T_ℓ(A)^∨ ⊗ Z_ℓ(1)'. The struck word before T_ℓ(A) is 'det' (deleted), and the dual applies to T_ℓ(A), not T_ℓ(A*).
In the definition of α_p, the field written '⊗ Q_ℓ' should be ⊗ Q_p.
'dans l'isom α_ℓ n'est autre que' is probably 'dans l'iso α_ℓ ... n'est autre que β_ℓ(φ)/deg φ'.
The crossed-out line before the lemma ('est trivialement formellement des cas') is illegible. The surviving word looks like 'formulable/formellement'.
